::: {#def-pearson-test}
#### Test of zero correlation

Let $r$ be the
[Pearson correlation coefficient](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-pearson-r)
of $n \ge 3$ pairs, with $\abs{r} < 1$.
The **t-test of zero correlation**
of $H_0: \corpar = 0$ against $H_1: \corpar \neq 0$
(@def-population-correlation) uses the statistic

$$t \eqdef \frac{r \sqrt{n - 2}}{\sqrt{1 - r^2}}.$$

Its p-value is $\Pr(\abs{T} \ge \abs{t})$,
where $T$ has the $t_{n-2}$ distribution ([t-distribution](inference.qmd#def-t-dist)).
:::
